promises.claim: Filing takes any balance from your accounts at once, the checking account first and then savings.

promises.claim: A balance your bank couldn’t pay at filing stays owed: the IRS’s bill comes at once, and its first reminder ${said(COLLECTION.noticeWeeks)} weeks after the deadline, or after filing if that’s later.
promises.holds: tax.file left owing sends the bill at once and the first reminder five weeks from the later of the due date and now (src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:1657; src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:406).

promises.claim: A refund is paid into your checking account ${RETURN.refundDays} days after filing, or ${ITIN_REFUND_DAYS} days on a 1040-NR filed without a Social Security number.
promises.holds: The refund 21 days on, seven weeks more on a 1040-NR without a Social Security number (src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:1642), paid to the payee account (src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:1503).

promises.claim: The Papers line on Home says when an unfiled return is due, what filing it would pay (including any late penalty), and the tax you owe.
promises.holds: Home’s Papers line reads the open return’s due date, what filing would pay with its late penalty, and the tax owed (src/ui/screens/Home.tsx:564).

promises.claim: On a 1040-NR, having a Social Security number before you file saves the ${said(SSN.itinWeeks)} weeks an ITIN application holds up the refund.
promises.holds: A 1040-NR filed without a Social Security number waits the ITIN’s weeks (src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:1641).

promises.claim: You owe a balance only on a filed return, or on one the IRS or a state assessed without you.
promises.holds: A balance is set only by filing, an assessment or an amendment (setOwed’s callers); Pay refuses a year not owed (src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:1671; src/engine/systems/statetax.ts:1007).

promises.claim: Each payment leaves your accounts at once, the checking account first and then savings.
promises.holds: tax.pay and tax.pay_state take the amount with payFromBank, checking then savings (src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:1677).

promises.claim: Paying a year in full moves its lien to Paid: Release To Come.
promises.holds: Paid in full, the IRS’s lien and a state’s go to paid (src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:278; src/engine/systems/statetax.ts:379).

promises.claim: If you leave it owing, a levy takes what your accounts hold on its day.
promises.holds: The IRS’s levy and a state’s take what the accounts hold (src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:1468; src/engine/systems/statetax.ts:991).

promises.claim: Tax owed weighs on you: each day ends with more stress and less morale until it’s paid.
promises.holds: Tax owed and a return past due are troubles (src/engine/systems/spending.ts:483), and each day of trouble adds stress and takes morale (src/engine/systems/spending.ts:508).

promises.claim: When you can’t pay at once, a plan stops collection for as long as you keep it up.
promises.holds: The IRS’s letters and levy wait while its plan stands (src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:1455); a state’s while its own does (src/engine/systems/statetax.ts:969).

promises.claim: Every return past its due date has to be filed before the IRS or a state sets up a plan.
promises.holds: planRefusal and statePlanRefusal refuse while a return is past due unfiled (src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:602; src/engine/systems/statetax.ts:469).

promises.claim: A plan being decided or in force stops the letters and the levy on what you owe.
promises.holds: A plan decided or in force holds the letters and the levy, and its start cancels those pending (src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:650).

promises.claim: While a state plan is in force, no lien is filed, and one that was only announced comes to nothing.
promises.holds: No lien step while a state plan stands, and a notice of intent comes to nothing under one (src/engine/systems/statetax.ts:666; src/engine/systems/statetax.ts:545).

promises.claim: Each plan payment is taken from your accounts on its day, every 30 days.
promises.holds: Each payment from the accounts on its day, the next 30 days on (src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:1553; src/engine/systems/statetax.ts:1177).

promises.claim: A Social Security number gets an IRS plan decided within a minute. Without one it takes ${PLAN.mailDays} days.
promises.holds: Online with a Social Security number the IRS decides in a minute; without, Form 9465 by mail in 30 days (src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:1522).

promises.claim: A lien is released only once what it was filed for is paid in full.
promises.holds: A state’s release is asked only once paid (src/engine/systems/statetax.ts:740); the IRS’s releases itself only on payment in full (src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:315).

promises.claim: A lien is withdrawn as filed in error only after your own return has replaced the assessment it was filed on.
promises.holds: A lien is in error only once their own return has replaced the assessment, and left nothing owed when it was filed (src/engine/systems/statetax.ts:764; src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:330).

promises.claim: While a state plan is in force, no lien is filed. Connecticut files its lien at its second notice.
promises.holds: No lien while a state plan stands (src/engine/systems/statetax.ts:666); Connecticut’s lien at its step 1, its second notice (content/statetax.ts, atStep 1).
